title: Why Eval++ Is the Next Great Compute Primitive — Sunil Pai & Matt Carey, Cloudflare
talk_summary: A Cloudflare fireside chat about their agent infrastructure: durable objects as stateful per-ID compute units, dynamic workers as an isolate-based sandbox for running LLM-generated code, and an agents SDK that gives resumable streaming and multi-client sync out of the box. It is mostly platform marketing with a few concrete architectural ideas (code mode, capability-scoped sandboxes, stateful resumable agent loops).

takeaways.technique: Capability-scoped isolate sandbox for generated code
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of starting from a VM/container and bolting on security, they start from a JS isolate with no fetch, no env vars, no APIs, and grant explicit capabilities from outside (e.g. only outgoing fetches to github.com).
takeaways.evidence_quote: The only thing you can run is JavaScript in it, but it has no access to fetch, no APIs, nothing. And from the outside you can decide, okay, here are like four APIs.

takeaways.technique: Stateful per-entity agent loop with resumable streaming
takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent instance is a durable object keyed by ID that persists across requests, hibernates, and can resume an in-flight stream when a client reconnects, instead of needing sticky sessions plus DB replication in userland.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you just reconnect to it and if there's a stream going on, it just says well, here's the beginning of the stream and I'm just going to continue giving you bytes

takeaways.technique: Code mode: generate code instead of JSON tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than emitting JSON that a DSL interprets, let the model write code that runs in a sandbox, which they claim lets one MCP server expose 2,600 API endpoints in ~1,000 tokens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how you can use code mode in your MCP server to give access to all 2,600 API endpoints of Cloudflare in just only 1,000 tokens

takeaways.technique: Generate UI/code directly rather than intermediate JSON
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues that generating JSON for a renderer is wasteful when you can generate HTML/React and render it in a sandbox, because the only blocker was a primitive to run untrusted code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Why are you generating JSON? Why don't you just generate HTML or even generate React and then just render that?

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents SDK lets you schedule recurring background work (e.g. every Friday compile git history and send a summary) that runs even with no incoming request.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every Friday at 9:00 p.m. look through my entire Git history and my uh wiki and the notion, compile it and send it to my manager
